title: Node.js Testing Handbook: node:test, Jest, Vitest, Mocks, supertest and Coverage
summary: Quick revision notes on testing Node.js apps: the built-in node:test runner with assert, Jest and Vitest, mocking modules and timers, testing HTTP handlers with supertest, database test doubles, and coverage.

chapters.title: Testing Node.js: Mental Model
points: A test file registers tests with describe/it (or test); the runner executes them, and a thrown error (usually from a failed assertion) marks the test failed
Arrange-Act-Assert: set up inputs, call the unit once, assert the outcome; one behavior per test
Unit tests isolate one module with test doubles; integration tests wire real pieces together (HTTP layer + real or in-memory DB)
Runner vs assertion library: the runner finds and runs tests and reports results; assertions (assert, expect) only throw on mismatch
Test behavior and public output, not internals: asserting on private calls makes tests break on every refactor

chapters.title: node:test and assert
points: Built in, no install: import { test, describe, it, before, after, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'node:test'; run with node --test (finds *.test.js and files under test/)
Use node:assert/strict: assert.equal is then ===, and assert.deepEqual is strict deep equality; the loose non-strict assert.equal uses ==
assert.throws(fn, /msg/) for sync errors; await assert.rejects(promise, { name: 'TypeError' }) for async errors; forgetting await passes the test falsely
Useful flags: --watch, --test-name-pattern='login', --experimental-test-coverage, --test-reporter=spec; async test functions are awaited automatically
t.mock.fn() and t.mock.method(obj, 'name') create spies that auto-restore after the test; t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout'] }) then t.mock.timers.tick(1000) fakes time

chapters.title: Jest vs Vitest
points: Both give describe/it/expect, matchers, mocks, snapshots and coverage out of the box; Vitest is Vite-powered, native ESM and TypeScript, and watches fast; Jest needs a transform (babel or ts-jest) for ESM/TS
Jest globals are automatic (jest.fn, jest.mock); Vitest globals need globals: true in config, otherwise import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'; the Vitest mock namespace is vi, not jest
Matchers: toBe is Object.is identity; toEqual is deep equality; toStrictEqual also checks undefined props and class types; toThrow needs the call wrapped in a function: expect(() => fn()).toThrow()
Async: await expect(p).resolves.toBe(1) and await expect(p).rejects.toThrow('x'); an un-awaited expect never fails the test; use expect.assertions(n) to guard
Commands: npx jest --watch, npx jest path -t 'name'; npx vitest (watch by default in a terminal), npx vitest run for one-shot CI mode

chapters.title: Mocking Modules and Timers
points: Spies observe, stubs replace return values, mocks add expectations; jest.fn() / vi.fn() with mockReturnValue, mockResolvedValue, mockImplementation, then assert with toHaveBeenCalledWith and toHaveBeenCalledTimes

jest.mock('./mailer') / vi.mock('./mailer') is hoisted above imports and replaces the module; the factory form is jest.mock('./mailer', () => ({ send: jest.fn() })), and Vitest factories must return the export shape, including default

Spy on a real method with jest.spyOn(obj, 'm') / vi.spyOn; restore with mockRestore or restoreMocks: true in config; call clearAllMocks (wipes calls) or resetAllMocks (wipes implementations) in afterEach so state does not leak between tests
Fake timers: jest.useFakeTimers() / vi.useFakeTimers(), then advanceTimersByTime(1000), runAllTimers(), and setSystemTime(date) for Date.now; always switch back with useRealTimers() in afterEach

Gotchas: ESM imports are static so mock before the import (vi.hoisted, or unstable_mockModule in Jest ESM); fake timers with awaited promises need the async variants (advanceTimersByTimeAsync); mocking too much means testing the mocks

chapters.title: HTTP Handlers, Database Doubles and Coverage
points: supertest: export the Express/Fastify app without calling listen(), then await request(app).post('/users').send({ name: 'a' }).set('Authorization', 'Bearer t').expect(201); it binds an ephemeral port itself
Assert status, body and headers: .expect(200), .expect('Content-Type', /json/), then check res.body; test the 400/401/404 error paths as well as the happy path

Database test doubles: a fake (in-memory repository, SQLite :memory:) keeps real behavior, a stub returns canned rows, a mock verifies calls; inject the repository as a dependency so a handler can be tested without a real DB

Real-DB integration tests: use a throwaway test database or Testcontainers, run migrations once, then wrap each test in a transaction and roll back, or truncate in beforeEach, so tests stay independent and order-free

Coverage: node --test --experimental-test-coverage, jest --coverage, vitest run --coverage (v8 or istanbul provider); it measures line, branch, function and statement execution, not correctness; set thresholds in CI, but high coverage with weak assertions proves little

chapters.title: Testing Cheat Sheet
points: Run: node --test | npx jest | npx vitest run; filter by name with --test-name-pattern or -t
Assert: node:assert/strict equal, deepEqual, throws, await rejects; Jest/Vitest toBe (identity), toEqual (deep), toStrictEqual, await expect().rejects
Mock: jest.fn()/vi.fn(), jest.mock()/vi.mock() (hoisted), spyOn with restore, clearAllMocks vs resetAllMocks vs restoreAllMocks
Time: useFakeTimers, advanceTimersByTime, setSystemTime, then useRealTimers; node:test uses t.mock.timers.tick
HTTP and DB: request(app) without listen, expect status/body/headers; inject repositories, roll back per test; Coverage: --coverage with thresholds, branch coverage matters most
